To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Distillation harms performance on certain sub-groups compared to the vanilla one-hot labels; (2) The problem is caused by errors made by the Teacher distribution being transferred to the student model; and (3) We propose modifications to distillation that maintain boost in overall performance while ensuring improvements in subgroup performance

distillation can harm the performance of subgroups, e. g., classes with few samples, compared to vanilla student training; this behavior is due to errors made by teachers being transferred to and then amplified by student models; and we present techniques which modify the teacher influence for such subgroups to mitigate this behavior, while maintaining boost in overall accuracy.

(i) knowledge distillation can hurt performance on certain sub-groups, (ii) this behavior is due to errors made by teacher distribution, and (iii) we can improve subgroup performance by reducing the teacher influence on those subgroups.

, while distillation is an effective tool for improving model performance, its use can be harmful to certain data subgroups.
the teacher’s influence on the student should be carefully considered when using distillation to improve performance of a student model.
distillation is not a panacea for improving the student’s performance on subgroups, and we must be mindful of its limitations and potential harms.
